summary: Built and filed the repair-path experiment for the question opened last turn. The cluster harness now runs a repair phase after the healed split state: it ensures a node holding the current configuration leads (transferring leadership to B if the healed leader is the stale node), disconnects the restarted node, commits ten further entries on that leader, takes a snapshot on it with TrailingLogs 0 so its log is compacted past the restarted node's position, reconnects the node, waits up to 15s for it to install a snapshot, and samples the conflict index and applied commands again. Local construction feedback was deterministic across three runs on every operand the comparisons use: the snapshot install occurs, the restarted node's applied write becomes majority-write, its minority-write disappears, the conflict index no longer exists in its log, and its reported configuration becomes {A,B,C,D,E}, while a node that stayed up to date keeps its minority write — so the six comparisons assert both halves of the answer, the ordinary recovery path repairing a node that falls behind a compacted leader, and per-node scope leaving an up-to-date divergent node unrepaired. Filing it as a new experiment under the repair-path question (rather than a previous_id revision) was required by the one-investigation rule for revisions; the harness lineage is described in the scope instead. Incomplete: that receipt and its interpretation, the no-feature restart control inside the cluster, and any longer window over the divergent state before repair.
